category_title: Students with disciplinary histories who identify as literacy 'connoisseurs'
scenario_title: Disengagement and authority resistance during 10th-grade English instruction
minimal_context: Yusef is participating in a 10th-grade English class where students are expected to read assigned books and complete regular class work.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Class, please continue reading the assigned book for today's lesson and complete the regular class work on your desks.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Closes the assigned book and turns to the class computer, beginning to surf the Internet) I already finished the book. It didn't take long.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Since you are done, please sit quietly and wait for the other students to finish.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Why do I have to wait for them? They're so slow. I'm not sitting here doing nothing just because they can't keep up. (Continues clicking on the computer, exhibiting a superior attitude toward classmates)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Yusef, you need to log off the computer and move back to your old seat right now. We will be having a meeting about this later.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm not going to any meeting and I'm not moving. I hate you. You're a bastard. (Crosses arms and completely refuses to talk anymore)
